title: Observer (behavioral)
points: A subject keeps a list of observers and broadcasts when something happens, expecting nothing back.
The subject doesn't know what observers do or how many there are. Each observer decides how to react.
Answers: who needs to know that this happened?
trade: Loose coupling (SRP, OCP). Downsides: harder to trace the flow, one failing listener can break others, forgotten unsubscribes leak memory, ordering and sync vs async need a decision. Spring @EventListener is this pattern.
test: OrderService.place(order) saves the order, then calls onOrderPlaced(order) on every subscribed OrderListener (for example EmailReceipt and InventoryUpdater). Why doesn't OrderService change when you add an SMS notification? Strategy vs Observer: which answers how and which answers who?
answer: The SMS notifier is just another listener subscribed to the service. Strategy answers how to do something; Observer answers who needs to know it happened.

questions.question: OrderService must tell email, inventory and analytics code that an order was placed, without knowing what they do. Which pattern fits?
questions.explanation: Observer: the subject broadcasts to subscribers and expects nothing back. Each observer decides how to react.
